subject: Agriculture
title: Peanuts and Groundnuts
description: Learn Peanuts and Groundnuts in one minute.

hook.text: Peanuts aren't nuts—they're legumes that bury their fruit underground. They fix nitrogen while producing food.

buildup.text: Originating in South America, peanuts spread globally via Portuguese and Spanish traders in the 1500s.

discovery.text: George Washington Carver promoted peanuts as a rotation crop to restore Southern US soils exhausted by cotton.

twist.text: Peanut allergies affect 2% of Western children and are increasing—the reason is still debated by scientists.

climax.text: In Africa and South Asia, peanuts provide critical protein where meat is scarce—they're a survival crop.

punchline.text: It's not a nut. It grows underground. And it feeds hundreds of millions.

quiz.question: Why did George Washington Carver promote peanut farming?
options: As a rotation crop to restore soil nitrogen depleted by cotton
